# Stemma – context for implementation

You implement one small slice. Everything binding is below. Open a file in `docs/` only when a section here points to it, and read only the referenced section.

## 1. Stack and layout

- Python 3.14, Django 5.2 LTS, SQLite (must not block a later PostgreSQL), Django templates + HTMX, minimal own JS, no SPA, no big JS framework (ACP-001, ACP-003, ACP-004).
- Apps in the repo root, no `src/`: `accounts` (users, permissions), `common` (shared choices, abstract models, validation, helpers), `people` (persons, names, categories, relationships), `places` (places, residences, grave sites), `events` (events, participants), `materials` (attachments, sources, links), `health` (health records). `audit` is planned only.
- Per app: `models.py`, `services.py` (writes), `selectors.py` (reads), `use_cases.py` (actor-aware orchestration), `forms.py`, `views.py`, `templates/`, tests as `test_*.py` next to the code.
- Shared UI: `people/templates/people/person_shell.html`, partials in `people/templates/people/partials/`, static `people/static/people/stemma.js` and `stemma.css`.
- User-facing text in Czech; stored choice values are stable English codes.

## 2. Domain rules (never break)

- Each fact, relationship, source and physical file is stored once. One marriage = one event linked to both persons; a relationship is stored once and shown both ways.
- Birth and death are events, not fields on a person (ACP-002). At most one active birth and one active death per person.
- Derived values (age, living/deceased, age at death, Roman numbering, reverse relationships, chronological order) are computed, not stored, unless an approved reason exists.
- Incomplete dates are never replaced by false precise dates. Supported: exact, year, month+year, approximate, before/after, range, unknown. A technical sort value for incomplete dates is allowed.
- Structured data beats free text (residence is a residence record, relationship is a relationship).
- Archiving and soft deletion are different lifecycle operations. Soft-deleted records are excluded from active computations. Lookup tables are deactivated, not deleted. Physical deletion is exceptional admin work. Deleting a link never deletes the attachment, source or target.
- Simpler solution wins when requirements are equal. No dependency without a clear, documented benefit.

## 3. Code placement

- Write business logic → `services.py`. Multi-object writes in `transaction.atomic()`.
- Complex reads (visibility, soft-delete filtering, `select_related`, `prefetch_related`, annotations) → `selectors.py`.
- Views only coordinate request, form, service/use-case and response. Templates never decide business integrity.
- Fixed validation/security values → `TextChoices`. User-extensible vocabularies → lookup models.
- Attachments and sources use explicit link models, never generic relations.
- Validation layers: DB constraints (required, FK, unique codes, simple checks, active duplicates, no self-relationship) → model `clean()` for single-object rules (remember `save()` does not call `full_clean()`) → domain services for cross-object rules.
- PEP 8, explicit, type-annotated code, short docstrings where they clarify responsibility. UTF-8, single trailing newline.

## 4. Security and privacy (server-side, always)

- Permissions are enforced on the server, never only by hiding UI. An action without permission is refused by the server too.
- Access follows the strictest restriction of all related objects. Health data and its attachments need special permissions; data of living persons has stricter defaults.
- ACP-007: a value derived for an actor may use only source records visible to that actor; hidden facts must not leak via age, living state, Roman numbering or empty-state differences. Unauthorized and nonexistent objects look the same (no existence leak).
- Never log or audit passwords, tokens, secrets or file contents.
- Files: Django Storage API; DB stores an opaque internal `storage_key` (never shown, never a URL or token); MIME not by extension only; SHA-256 after upload; direct file URLs must not bypass permissions.
- ACP-012 (attachments): each user has exactly one `Vault`; an `Attachment` belongs to one Vault and its owner is `attachment.vault.owner`; `private` attachments are readable only by the active owner (or a future explicit grant); authorization always combines target policy + link + attachment. `PlaceAttachment` and `AttachmentSource` stay fail-closed without a general selector.
- Health lifecycle (ACP-010, ACP-011): states ACTIVE / ARCHIVED / SOFT_DELETED, never both timestamps set; only the explicitly named operations `archive_health_record`, `restore_archived_health_record`, `soft_delete_health_record`, `restore_soft_deleted_health_record`; no generic `restore`/`delete`.

## 5. UI and HTMX

- ACP-008: stable global shell; root URL is the Overview; sections Přehled, Osoby, Rodokmen, Dokumenty, Místa, Materiály / zdroje, Můj prostor. Osoby = list on the left, detail on the right; on mobile they are separate layers. Unimplemented areas are clearly marked as planned and never show fake data.
- Server returns full HTML or fragments; HTMX endpoints return a consistent fragment with the correct HTTP status; support both full-page and HTMX modes where the existing view does.
- Form errors appear at the field and where the user works (error summary gets focus).
- Keep accessibility attributes (`aria-expanded`, `aria-current`, focus handling) consistent with behaviour.

## 6. Migrations

- Only when models, fields, constraints, indexes or required data state change. Small and readable; separate structural and data migrations when clearer.
- Never rewrite a migration already in the shared branch; fix with a new one. No intentional data loss.

## 7. Tests

- New or changed behaviour gets tests. Run focused tests while working: `.venv/bin/python manage.py test <app>.<module>`.
- Integrity areas that must stay covered: person without names, incomplete dates and sorting, one active birth/death, required event roles, symmetric/directional relationships, parent cycles, one main photo, soft delete/restore, health protection, files and checksums.
- For authorization changes test anonymous, authenticated, inactive, staff and object-visibility cases.
- JavaScript-only behaviour cannot be tested by Django tests; if a browser check is needed, keep it a standalone script outside Django discovery (not named `test*.py`) and say in the changelog how to run it.

## 8. Scope and approvals

- RC 0.2 works on `agent/rc-0.2`. Approved so far: read-only person tabs (relationships, residences, grave sites, events), person PDF/A4 export, materials browsing and upload, person creation, search, narrow birth/death create/edit, attachment delivery (M3.4).
- NOT approved without explicit user approval: Relationship / Residence / GraveSite / PersonGraveSite write or lifecycle UI, general Event detail, general Event/participant write UI, Place management, general Materials UI, new ACPs, architecture changes. If a task seems to require them, stop and explain.

## 10. Finishing a task

1. Focused tests green, then review your whole diff once (scope, accidental weakening, stray files).
2. Add `docs/changelog/YYYY-MM-DD-<short-name>.md` (Czech, for humans, template `docs/changelog/_sablona.md`).
3. Commit with explicit paths. Do not push; the workflow checks run next and Cezar opens the PR.
